candidates.title: Beyond the tool: a systematic realist synthesis of cognitive agency in human-GenAI interaction in higher education
candidates.reason: Tracks student verification of AI outputs and whether students can later work independently.
candidates.prior_index_note: Original-publication day unresolved in the historical catalog.

candidates.title: Motivational gain trumps cognitive offloading: a MASEM study on the net positive effect of AI use on critical thinking
candidates.reason: Pools evidence on opposing associations of motivation and dependence with critical thinking.

candidates.title: Utilizing a GPT-based exam assistant to support practice and assessment in higher education: an exploratory study on learner engagement and perceptions
candidates.reason: Interaction logs distinguish opening an assistant from answering its questions.

candidates.title: Beyond the Pyramid: Bloom’s Taxonomy Meets Generative AI
candidates.reason: Uses a teaching example to examine judgment exercised after AI supplies a finished explanation.

candidates.title: The epistemic limits of generative AI disclosure in scholarly authorship
candidates.reason: Proposes a test of whether provenance labels divert attention from the argument in a manuscript.

candidates.title: Performance without capability: generative AI and the validity of assessment in higher education
candidates.reason: Explores what an assessor can infer from an AI-assisted assignment and its process record.

candidates.title: For students and teachers, AI is forcing a conversation about how to learn and teach in an AI world
candidates.reason: Interviews describe a student using revision feedback and instructors bringing writing back into class.

candidates.title: AI Has a Place in Education, Just Not in My Classroom
candidates.reason: A teacher explains how independent literacy practice shapes a classroom decision about AI.

candidates.title: Deploying AI into workplaces: What leaders need to know
candidates.date_evidence: Publication date confirmed with publisher release; the guidance is a separate full report.
candidates.reason: Objectives 4 and 5 address checking workload and preserving practice for novice workers.

candidates.title: Generative artificial intelligence dependence and academic performance: serial mediation through attentional control and physical fitness and moderation by grade level
candidates.date_evidence: Publisher's Published field, distinguished from its earlier acceptance date
candidates.reason: School survey on dependence, attentional control and academic performance.

candidates.title: A study on the relationships among perceived cognitive offloading, cognitive load allocation, and academic engagement in AI-empowered curriculum environments
candidates.date_evidence: Publisher's Published field, distinguished from its earlier acceptance date
candidates.reason: A student survey distinguishes checking effort from effort spent integrating and learning material.

candidates.title: Survey of the impacts of generative artificial intelligence on critical thinking development in education
candidates.reason: The 66-study review overlaps with the selected Li review. The open article-in-press PDF was checked.

candidates.title: AI usage, large language model dependence, and critical thinking among university students: the mediating roles of metacognitive awareness and AI literacy
candidates.reason: Useful corroboration from self-report, but the selected meta-analysis already examines reliance and critical thinking.

candidates.title: Human tutoring, generative AI tutoring and independent internet search: A randomised between-subjects experiment on students' responses to academic challenge
candidates.reason: Search results surfaced the article this week. Wiley gives a first-publication date before the window.

candidates.title: Study finds no learning difference between AI tutoring modes for adults
candidates.reason: Followed the DOI to arXiv:2610.26411, an October preprint. The new summary does not make it new original research.

candidates.title: AI is imposing a hidden ‘cognitive tax’ on the lowest-paid workers
candidates.reason: Henrietta Moore argues unpredictable AI scheduling can add to the burden of economic insecurity and advocates universal basic services. It offers a different emphasis from the edition's account of oversight and practice; it does not measure an effect on attention.

candidates.title: As AI Changes How Students Approach College, Old Challenges Persist
candidates.reason: The article text was visible in search retrieval but carried an institutional access notice. Eligibility for free access remains unresolved.

candidates.title: How AI Is Changing the Way Employees Spend Time at Work
candidates.reason: Follow-up to the prior week's dated lead. This report deals with time use and output expectations. It did not supply a source for the selected eleven-source editorial.

remaining_work: The automated closeout retained 25 unfinished provider queries. Additional verified late-indexed articles can be considered for this edition.

The search concentrated on education, evaluation and work. Outlet-by-outlet coverage is incomplete. A targeted Conversation lookup was blocked, and the Inside Higher Ed item's open-access status is unresolved.

The eight scholarly sources consist of three conceptual articles, two research syntheses, one classroom comparison and two cross-sectional studies. The three nonacademic sources are reporting, a practitioner's argument and guidance. The adolescent study measured attention by questionnaire; the classroom study used interaction logs.
